newsitem.title: USA: Yurie Systems raises IPO price range.
newsitem.headline: Yurie Systems raises IPO price range.

text.p: Yurie Systems Inc raised the price tag for shares of its initial public offering to $10 to $11 a share, according to a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

The four million shares, originally been estimated to price at $10 to $11, are due to price later today for trading tomorrow on the Nasdaq under the symbol "YURI", said lead underwriter Alex Brown & Sons Inc.
The company makes asynchronous transfer mode ("ATM") products for telecommunications service providers, corporate end users and government end users.

The IPO has been scoring high marks with analysts for both short- and long-term gains. Vince Slavin, who tracks IPOs for Cantor Fitzgerald, gives the deal an 'A+' rating and says it could reap opening premiums of at least a point or more after its market debut.

Manish Shah, editor of the IPO Maven, says the company is a good long-term bet. "It's going to be volatile. But hang on to it for about 12 months. There's not much downside here," he said when the deal was priced at $8 to $10 a share.
Lanham, Maryland-based Yurie will sell all the shares being offered, which represent about 16 percent of the company.

Its technology allows users to integrate high performance communications technology into existing systems without scrapping all their old equipment. The systems also function with copper wire, eliminating the need for an expensive upgrade to fiber optics.

The IPO Insider newsletter recommends the IPO on the basis of the promise of its products, which "overrides some weaknesses of the company," including its limited operating history. The company was founded in 1992.

The newsletter also cited growing global demand for communications services and a key pact struck with AT&T Corp to distributes Yurie's products in certain markets and gives it about $10 million in annual revenues.
Based on its performance in the nine months in 1996, "we forecast fully diluted 1996 earnings per share of $0.15, which at a share price of $10 yields a price/earnings ratio of 67," it said.
